scope: Sources fetched and checked for the venue-record section of the orbital AI networking survey. Every identity named in that section but absent from paper-corpus.json appears here with the page or DOI that confirms it, and with the tier at which the section is allowed to cite it.

tier_definitions.programme-verified: Exact title string found in an official programme or accepted-paper page fetched on the record date. Venue, year and existence are established; the primary text was not reviewed to the corpus standard.
tier_definitions.doi-verified: Title, container and year resolved through DOI content negotiation against Crossref on the record date.
tier_definitions.standard: A published standards document fetched in full from the issuing body.
tier_definitions.reported-number: A quantity taken from the primary text of a paper that has no reviewed record in paper-corpus.json. The number was read from the source named in the entry, but it did not pass the corpus's full extraction and cross-check, so it carries lower assurance than any number quoted from a corpus record.

entries.group: large models over a satellite link

items.title: A Satellite-Ground Synergistic Large Vision-Language Model System for Earth Observation
items.container: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia
reported: A 2-billion-parameter model runs onboard and a 7-billion-parameter model on the ground, with a learned confidence network choosing between them.
The authors measure their own commercial Starlink terminal at an average of 110.67 Mbps.
The contact window is stated as an average 4.33% of the orbital period.

items.title: Enabling Near-realtime Remote Sensing via Satellite-Ground Collaboration of Large Vision-Language Models
items.container: Proceedings of the 2026 ACM/IEEE International Conference on Embedded Artificial Intelligence and Sensing Systems
reported: Mean end-to-end latency of 6.3 s and 7.9 s on two remote-sensing question-answering datasets.
An onboard distilled archive capped at 20 images is refreshed during the contact window.

items.title: Schedule-Aware Bundle Routing
quoted_definitions: route: a sequence of contacts such that the time at which contact i+1 ends is no earlier than the time at which contact i begins
volume: of a contact, the product of its duration and its data transmission rate

items.evidence: Call text lists 'Distributed KV-cache architectures' as a topic and states that 'inference requires distributed KV cache capacity under strict tail latency constraints'.
Call text names 'long context inference (KV cache transfer and offloading)'.
Programme lists 'ARK: Avoiding Routing Collisions for KV Cache Transfer in Disaggregated LLM Inference'.

entries.group: preprint-tier occupants of the state question

items.title: SkyMemory: A LEO Edge Cache for Transformer Inference Optimization and Scale Out
reported: A 21% token-generation speedup with one quantizer and about 24% with another, on a 1.1-billion-parameter model on an embedded board.
One prompt's key-value cache is striped across satellites and keyed by block hash and chunk identifier.

items.title: ImpactHO: Importance-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Multi-User Edge LLM Handover
reported: Over 93.7% average accuracy within a 500 ms transfer window, within 0.5 percentage points of the full-cache ceiling.
391 ms average handover latency against 847 ms for recomputing the cache from the text.
The transport is terrestrial backhaul at 20 Gbps by default, swept from 10 to 30 Gbps.

items.title: Iapetus: Content-Aware Hierarchical Scheduling for Collaborative ViT Inference in LEO Satellite Networks
reported: Per-layer token pruning and placement are planned jointly; inter-satellite bandwidth is an assumed parameter rather than a measurement.

items.title: In-Orbit Intelligence or Ground Offloading? Inference Freshness under Intermittent Satellite Connectivity

number_policy: Numbers attached to entries in this file carry the reported-number tier: they were read from the named source but have no reviewed record in paper-corpus.json. The survey page states this where it quotes them, and a claim that depends on one of these numbers should re-read the primary text first.
